slides.name: Which curls deserve a spot in your routine?

placements.value:
An awkward grip without much payoff.
Regular curls are easier to set up and add weight to.

Useful for forearm work and grip variety.
A lower priority if biceps growth is your main goal.

Chest support helps keep your reps honest.
The bench setup can be a hassle.

Your biceps work hard, but so does your back.
Great for pulling strength, less targeted than a curl.

A simple curl that's easy to add weight to over time.
Keep your torso still as the reps get harder.

A simple, accessible staple.
Sit tall and control the weight on the way down.

Your biceps work here, too.
A useful neutral-grip option to pair with palms-up curls.

The bench helps keep swinging in check.
Choose an angle that feels good on your shoulders.

Easy to adjust. Easy to keep reps consistent.
Pulley position changes where the curl feels hardest.

The arm support makes progress easier to track.
Lower with control and keep your arms on the pad.

A solid cable option with your arm behind your body.
Feeling a stretch doesn't automatically make it the best.

Train each arm separately with solid support.
Let your weaker arm set the rep count.

Stable setup. Easy weight changes. Consistent reps.
A top pick if the machine fits you well.
